{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# RSpec Performance Optimization

This document tracks profiling metrics, identified root causes, shared RSpec infrastructure/tags, and plans for subsequent optimization phases (`spec/requests` and `spec/fabricators`).

---

## Phase 1: `spec/models` & Shared Test Infrastructure

### Baseline vs. Optimized Metrics (`spec/models`)

| Metric | Baseline | After Phase 1 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spec files / Examples | 152 files / 1,795 examples | 152 files / 1,795 examples | 0 failures |
| Wall-clock runtime (`--seed 12345`) | **132.3s** (2m 12.3s) | **30.3s** (avg ~31.8s across seeds) | **~76% faster (~4.2x)** |
| `sql.active_record` events | 113,956 queries | < 45,000 queries | > 60% reduction |
| Factory calls (`FactoryProf`) | 4,721 total (114.6s) | 2,869 total (25.5s) | ~78% less factory time |
| `log/test.log` written per run | ~65 MB | ~0 KB | Eliminated |

#### Slowest Model Spec Groups: Before vs. After

| Spec File | Baseline | After Phase 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/models/account_statuses_cleanup_policy_spec.rb` (36 ex) | 11.49s | < 0.40s |
| `spec/models/trends/statuses_spec.rb` (12 ex) | 11.26s | < 0.40s (per-example) / ~0.9s total |
| `spec/models/tag_feed_spec.rb` (33 ex) | 10.22s | < 0.40s |
| `spec/models/status_spec.rb` (62 ex) | 10.06s | ~2.7s |
| `spec/models/notification_spec.rb` (25 ex) | 6.74s | ~0.7s |
| `spec/models/public_feed_spec.rb` (43 ex) | 6.52s | ~0.7s |
| `spec/models/media_attachment_spec.rb` (27 ex) | 5.55s | ~4.1s |
| `spec/models/concerns/status/threading_concern_spec.rb` (16 ex) | 5.45s | ~0.4s |
| `spec/models/account_spec.rb` (111 ex) | 4.77s | ~1.7s |
| `spec/models/concerns/account/interactions_spec.rb` (71 ex) | 4.53s | ~1.0s |
| `spec/models/concerns/status/fetch_replies_concern_spec.rb` (15 ex) | 3.71s | < 0.40s |
| `spec/models/user_spec.rb` (61 ex) | 3.21s | ~0.8s |
| `spec/models/form/import_spec.rb` (93 ex) | 2.98s | < 0.40s |

---

### Root Causes Identified & Fixed in Phase 1

1. **Accidental `ActiveRecord.verbose_query_logs = true` & `:debug` Logging (~35.6% / 45.6s of baseline)**
   - `spec/models/concerns/status/fetch_replies_concern_spec.rb` had a top-level `ActiveRecord.verbose_query_logs = true` statement evaluated at file-load time, enabling `Rails::BacktraceCleaner` stack-walk on every SQL query across the entire RSpec process.
   - `config/environments/test.rb` left `config.log_level` at `:debug` (and `HttpLog` / `Paperclip` logging enabled), formatting binds, ANSI-coloring SQL, and writing ~65 MB to `log/test.log` per `spec/models` run.
   - **Fix**: Removed stray `ActiveRecord.verbose_query_logs = true`; configured `config.log_level = ENV.fetch('RAILS_LOG_LEVEL', :warn)`, `Paperclip.options[:log] = false`, and `HttpLog.config.enabled = false` in `config/environments/test.rb`.

2. **Global `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` & ActiveJob Queue Adapter (~24.5% / 31.4s of baseline)**
   - `spec/rails_helper.rb` forced `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` on every example. As a result, model `after_commit` hooks (`TriggerWebhookWorker` on every `User`, `Account`, `Status`, and `Report` create/update, plus `MailDeliveryJob` / timeline / notification workers) executed synchronously. `TriggerWebhookWorker#perform` alone consumed **23.4% (30.0s)** of `spec/models` re-querying records and serializing full `REST::StatusSerializer` / `REST::Admin::AccountSerializer` payloads for zero enabled webhooks.
   - **Fix**:
     - Set `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :test` in `config/environments/test.rb` so `deliver_later` enqueues lightweight test jobs without rendering templates during unrelated setup, while `ActionMailer::TestHelper#capture_emails` (both positive and negative email assertions) works natively without requiring inline Sidekiq.
     - Changed `spec/rails_helper.rb` so `type: :model` defaults to `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)`, with explicit `sidekiq: :inline` / `sidekiq: :fake` metadata tag support.

3. **Unnecessary Paperclip Style Processing (`spec/support/paperclip.rb`, `:paperclip_processing` tag)**
   - Every `MediaAttachment`, `CustomEmoji`, `PreviewCard`, `Avatar`, and `Header` assignment ran `vips`, `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`, and `blurhash` post-processing (~8% of post-Sidekiq runtime) even in specs only testing SQL scopes, batch forms, or validations.
   - **Fix**: Added `spec/support/paperclip.rb` to skip `Paperclip::Attachment#post_process_styles` for `type: :model` unless `:paperclip_processing` metadata is set (keeping `before_file_validate` callbacks intact). Tagged `Account::Avatar`, `Account::Header`, and format-processing groups in `media_attachment_spec.rb` with `:paperclip_processing`.

4. **Redundant Materialized View Refreshes (`spec/support/domain_materializable.rb`, `:refresh_instances_view` tag)**
   - `DomainMaterializable#refresh_instances_view` ran `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY instances` + Redis HyperLogLog commands on every remote `Account` / `DomainBlock` / `DomainAllow` creation, while only 3 example groups in `spec/mo",
  "output_tail": "resh_instances_view` (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY instances`) |
| `:rack_attack` | `:request` | Disabled (`false`), except `described_class == Rack::Attack` | Enable `Rack::Attack` throttling/blocklist middleware during request specs |

---

## Future Phase Plan: Phase 3 — Factories (`spec/fabricators/`)

*(Do not apply until the dedicated factory optimization phase.)*

Even after Phases 1 and 2, `FactoryProf` shows that `Fabricate` still accounts for **25.5s / 31.9s (~80%)** of `spec/models` (2,869 calls) and **21.7s / 49.8s (~44%)** of `spec/requests` (3,899 calls), largely due to unnecessary cascading associations and `after_create` callbacks in core fabricators:

1. **`spec/fabricators/status_fabricator.rb` (Top priority!)**
   - Lines 10–12 unconditionally run:
     ```ruby
     after_create do |status|
       Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status)
     end
     ```
   - `Fabricate(:bookmark)` in turn runs `account { Fabricate.build(:account) }` -> `user { Fabricate.build(:user) }` -> `2.times { Fabricate(:login_activity) }`!
   - Thus **every single `Fabricate(:status)` secretly creates a `Bookmark`, a second `Account`, a second `User`, a second `Keypair`, and 2 extra `LoginActivity` rows**!
   - Impact measured by `FactoryProf`:
     - `spec/models`: 441 of 445 bookmarks came from this hook (costing **5.4s** post-Phase-1).
     - `spec/requests`: 339 of 348 bookmarks came from this hook (costing **3.8s** post-Phase-2, and accounting for >55% of `Fabricate(:status)`'s 7.0s cost).

# RSpec Performance Optimization

This document tracks profiling metrics, identified root causes, shared RSpec infrastructure/tags, and plans for subsequent optimization phases (`spec/requests` and `spec/fabricators`).

---

## Phase 1: `spec/models` & Shared Test Infrastructure

### Baseline vs. Optimized Metrics (`spec/models`)

| Metric | Baseline | After Phase 1 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spec files / Examples | 152 files / 1,795 examples | 152 files / 1,795 examples | 0 failures |
| Wall-clock runtime (`--seed 12345`) | **132.3s** (2m 12.3s) | **30.3s** (avg ~31.8s across seeds) | **~76% faster (~4.2x)** |
| `sql.active_record` events | 113,956 queries | < 45,000 queries | > 60% reduction |
| Factory calls (`FactoryProf`) | 4,721 total (114.6s) | 2,869 total (25.5s) | ~78% less factory time |
| `log/test.log` written per run | ~65 MB | ~0 KB | Eliminated |

#### Slowest Model Spec Groups: Before vs. After

| Spec File | Baseline | After Phase 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/models/account_statuses_cleanup_policy_spec.rb` (36 ex) | 11.49s | < 0.40s |
| `spec/models/trends/statuses_spec.rb` (12 ex) | 11.26s | < 0.40s (per-example) / ~0.9s total |
| `spec/models/tag_feed_spec.rb` (33 ex) | 10.22s | < 0.40s |
| `spec/models/status_spec.rb` (62 ex) | 10.06s | ~2.7s |
| `spec/models/notification_spec.rb` (25 ex) | 6.74s | ~0.7s |
| `spec/models/public_feed_spec.rb` (43 ex) | 6.52s | ~0.7s |
| `spec/models/media_attachment_spec.rb` (27 ex) | 5.55s | ~4.1s |
| `spec/models/concerns/status/threading_concern_spec.rb` (16 ex) | 5.45s | ~0.4s |
| `spec/models/account_spec.rb` (111 ex) | 4.77s | ~1.7s |
| `spec/models/concerns/account/interactions_spec.rb` (71 ex) | 4.53s | ~1.0s |
| `spec/models/concerns/status/fetch_replies_concern_spec.rb` (15 ex) | 3.71s | < 0.40s |
| `spec/models/user_spec.rb` (61 ex) | 3.21s | ~0.8s |
| `spec/models/form/import_spec.rb` (93 ex) | 2.98s | < 0.40s |

### Root Causes Identified & Fixed in Phase 1

1. **Accidental `ActiveRecord.verbose_query_logs = true` & `:debug` Logging (~35.6% / 45.6s of baseline)**
   - `spec/models/concerns/status/fetch_replies_concern_spec.rb` had a top-level `ActiveRecord.verbose_query_logs = true` statement evaluated at file-load time, enabling `Rails::BacktraceCleaner` stack-walk on every SQL query across the entire RSpec process.
   - `config/environments/test.rb` left `config.log_level` at `:debug` (and `HttpLog` / `Paperclip` logging enabled), formatting binds, ANSI-coloring SQL, and writing ~65 MB to `log/test.log` per `spec/models` run.
   - **Fix**: Removed stray `ActiveRecord.verbose_query_logs = true`; configured `config.log_level = ENV.fetch('RAILS_LOG_LEVEL', :warn)`, `Paperclip.options[:log] = false`, and `HttpLog.config.enabled = false` in `config/environments/test.rb`.

2. **Global `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` & ActiveJob Queue Adapter (~24.5% / 31.4s of baseline)**
   - `spec/rails_helper.rb` forced `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` on every example. As a result, model `after_commit` hooks (`TriggerWebhookWorker` on every `User`, `Account`, `Status`, and `Report` create/update, plus `MailDeliveryJob` / timeline / notification workers) executed synchronously. `TriggerWebhookWorker#perform` alone consumed **23.4% (30.0s)** of `spec/models` re-querying records and serializing full `REST::StatusSerializer` / `REST::Admin::AccountSerializer` payloads for zero enabled webhooks.
   - **Fix**:
     - Set `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :test` in `config/environments/test.rb` so `deliver_later` enqueues lightweight test jobs without rendering templates during unrelated setup, while `ActionMailer::TestHelper#capture_emails` (both positive and negative email assertions) works natively without requiring inline Sidekiq.
     - Changed `spec/rails_helper.rb` so `type: :model` defaults to `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)`, with explicit `sidekiq: :inline` / `sidekiq: :fake` metadata tag support.

3. **Unnecessary Paperclip Style Processing (`spec/support/paperclip.rb`, `:paperclip_processing` tag)**
   - Every `MediaAttachment`, `CustomEmoji`, `PreviewCard`, `Avatar`, and `Header` assignment ran `vips`, `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`, and `blurhash` post-processing (~8% of post-Sidekiq runtime) even in specs only testing SQL scopes, batch forms, or validations.
   - **Fix**: Added `spec/support/paperclip.rb` to skip `Paperclip::Attachment#post_process_styles` for `type: :model` unless `:paperclip_processing` metadata is set (keeping `before_file_validate` callbacks intact). Tagged `Account::Avatar`, `Account::Header`, and format-processing groups in `media_attachment_spec.rb` with `:paperclip_processing`.

4. **Redundant Materialized View Refreshes (`spec/support/domain_materializable.rb`, `:refresh_instances_view` tag)**
   - `DomainMaterializable#refresh_instances_view` ran `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY instances` + Redis HyperLogLog commands on every remote `Account` / `DomainBlock` / `DomainAllow` creation, while only 3 example groups in `spec/mo

Investigate whether `Account` fabricator needs `user` by default or if `User` validation/callbacks can be streamlined in fabricators.

  end

  silenced_at           { |attrs| attrs[:silenced] ? Time.now.utc : nil }

  uri                   { |attrs| attrs[:domain].nil? ? nil : "https://#{attrs[:domain]}/users/#{attrs[:username]}" }
  discoverable          true
  indexable             true

  # This is not strictly needed but this avoids generating multiple keys
  # and, when `store_private_key` is passed, stores private keys for use in request specs
  keypairs do |attrs|

          uri: attrs[:domain].nil? ? nil : "https://#{attrs[:domain]}/users/#{attrs[:username]}#main-key",
          local_fragment: attrs[:domain].nil? ? '#main-key' : nil
        ),
      ]
    end
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Fabrication Performance in Our Tests**

Okay, let's dive deep into this performance issue. I'm going to run `FPROF=1 EVENT_PROF=sql.active_record` on `spec/requests --seed 12345`. And I need to verify how `Fabricate.build` behaves, specifically in relation to profiling. Does `FactoryProf` track `Fabricate.build` at all? Let's check the data.

Looking at the `FactoryProf` table, I see some interesting numbers. `status` is at 442 calls in total, with 398 top-level calls. `bookmark` has 445 total calls with only 4 at the top level. `account` is at 661 calls, with 607 top-level calls, and `user` shows 93 total with 84 at top-level calls. I'm also seeing `login_activity` at 256 calls, but none at the top level.

Wait a minute, these numbers are telling a story. I see that `bookmark` is being called 445 times via `Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status)`. Inside `bookmark_fabricator.rb`, it is set up to build instances of both `account` and `status` using `Fabricate.build`. This suggests that the bookmark is calling `Fabricate.build(:account)` 441 times. And I can see that `account` is then calling `Fabricate.build(:user)` 1,100+ times!

Aha! `FactoryProf` only hooks `Fabricate.create` (i.e., `Fabricate(...)`), not `Fabricate.build(...)`. Because when ActiveRecord saves `Bookmark` or `Account`, it cascades `save` to those `Fabricate.build(:account)` and `Fabricate.build(:user)` calls, which *still* trigger ActiveRecord validations, callbacks, and database inserts. I'm talking about inserts into `accounts`, `users`, and `keypairs`!

Now, the `login_activity` count of 256 is key. The `after_create` hook in `Fabricator(:user)` is a fabrication hook that only triggers on `Fabricate(:user)` or `Fabricate(:admin_user)`. That means it's running 93 + 33 + 6 = 132 * 2 which is approximately 256, NOT on the `Fabricate.build(:user)` calls when saved by ActiveRecord.

This explains why `Fabricate.build(:account)` -> `Fabricate.build(:user)` is such a bottleneck. Each `Fabricate(:status)` call is:

1.  Calling `Fabricate.build(:account)` (if `account:` wasn't passed), and that, in turn, calls `Fabricate.build(:user, account: nil)` and `Keypair.new(...)`. And when `status` saves, ActiveRecord saves `account`, `user`, and `keypair`.
2.  Then, the `after_create` in `status` calls `Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status)`, which recursively calls `Fabricate.build(:account)`, `Fabricate.build(:user, account: nil)`, `Keypair.new(...)`, saving `bookmark`, `account`, `user`, and `keypair`.

*   `Fabrication::Generator::Base#persist` is responsible for a massive **19,021 samples (53.7%)**. That's where we are saving records and dealing with cascading associations which is expected to be expensive, but it still seems quite high.
*   `Fabrication::Generator::Base#build` clocks in at **7,632 samples (21.5%)**, which includes the attribute building and calls to `Fabricate.build`.

ActiveRecord::Base.connection.begin_transaction(joinable: false)
begin
  [:account, :remote_account, :user, :admin_user, :status].each do |fab|
    queries = []

  end
ensure

end

messages.thinking:
**Database Query Bottleneck Investigation**

Okay, hold on a second! Just *look* at these query counts for `Fabricate(:account)` and `Fabricate(:status)`! This is a goldmine for optimization, especially after that initial warm-up time which, thankfully, we can ignore for now. Let's dig in. I'm seeing a concerning number of queries, especially when considered in a repeated testing context.

Let's dissect `Fabricate(:account)` query by query to understand the root cause. Okay, here we go:

*   Query 3: A check for an existing `keypair` with a `local_fragment` but no `account_id`. Makes sense for uniqueness.
*   Query 4: A username/domain check. Seems related to uniqueness as well.
*   Query 5: A check against `username_blocks`. Looks like validation. This is probably due to the `Account` validation via `UsernameBlockValidator`
*   Query 6: The actual `INSERT` into the `accounts` table. Finally, the account is created.
*   Query 7: Another `keypair` uniqueness check! It's repeated but this time, it's checking for the `account_id` this time. This is inefficient; the check ran before the creation, then we are checking again *after* the account is created.
*   Query 8: An `INSERT` into `keypairs`.
*   Queries 9 and 10: Retrieving `UserRole.everyone` *twice*! We are querying the same thing, again. This is likely an eager loading issue.
*   Query 11: Email uniqueness check on the `users` table. Validation.
*   Queries 12, 13, and 16: Fetching `settings` records. A lot of these queries are duplicated.
*   Query 14: Checking for `email_domain_blocks`. This also seems related to validation.
*   Query 15: Another `username_block` check but this time, checking for `allow_with_approval` as `true`. More validation.
*   Query 17: Finally, an `INSERT` into `users`!

Looking at this, it's clear we have some serious inefficiencies and redundancies. I'm seeing multiple repeated database hits for things that should either be cached, or batched, or validated more efficiently. We have redundant checks and multiple lookups for the same records. It's time to examine the relevant models (`Account`, `User`, `Status`, `Keypair`) to pinpoint the exact locations of these queries and understand why they are so chatty with the database. We need to streamline the validation, consider eager loading to reduce the number of queries, and optimize the overall data creation process.

  end

  ActiveRecord::Base.connection.rollback_transaction
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# == Schema Information
#
# Table name: keypairs
#
#  id             :bigint(8)        not null, primary key
#  expires_at     :datetime
#  local_fragment :string
#  private_key    :string
#  public_key     :string           not null
#  revoked        :boolean          default(FALSE), not null
#  type           :integer          not null
#  uri            :string
#  created_at     :datetime         not null
#  updated_at     :datetime         not null
#  account_id     :bigint(8)        not null
#

class Keypair < ApplicationRecord
  include Expireable

  self.inheritance_column = nil

  encrypts :private_key

  belongs_to :account

  enum :type, {
    rsa: 0,
    ed25519: 1,
    'ml-dsa-44': 2,
  }, validate: true

  validates :uri, presence: true, uniqueness: true, if: -> { account.remote? }
  validates :uri, absence: true, if: -> { account.local? }

  validates :local_fragment, presence: true, uniqueness: { scope: :account_id }, format: { with: /\A#[A-Z0-9-]+\Z/i }, if: -> { account.local? }
  validates :local_fragment, absence: true, if: -> { account.remote? }

  validates :public_key, presence: true
  validates :private_key, presence: true, if: -> { account.local? }
  validates :private_key, absence: true, if: -> { account.remote? }

  scope :unexpired, -> { where(expires_at: nil).or(where.not(expires_at: ..Time.now.utc)) }
  scope :usable, -> { unexpired.where(revoked: false) }

  alias actor account

  def full_uri
    return ActivityPub::TagManager.instance.uri_for(account) + local_fragment if local_fragment.present?

    uri
  end

  def keypair
    @keypair ||= begin
      case type
      when 'rsa'
        OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.new(private_key || public_key)
      when 'ed25519', 'ml-dsa-44'
        OpenSSL::PKey.read(private_key || public_key)
      end
    end
  end

  def linzer_public_key
    @linzer_public_key ||= begin
      case type
      when 'rsa'
        Linzer.new_rsa_v1_5_sha256_public_key(public_key)
      when 'ed25519'
        Linzer.new_ed25519_public_key(public_key)
      end
    end
  end

  def linzer_private_key
    @linzer_private_key ||= begin
      case type
      when 'rsa'
        Linzer.new_rsa_v1_5_sha256_key(private_key, full_uri)
      when 'ed25519'
        Linzer.new_ed25519_key(private_key, full_uri)
      end
    end
  end

  def usable?
    !revoked? && !expired?
  end

  def self.from_keyid(uri)
    return if uri.blank?

    keypair = find_by(uri: uri)
    return keypair unless keypair.nil?

    # No keypair found, try the old way we used to store RSA keypairs
    account = ActivityPub::TagManager.instance.uri_to_actor(uri)
    return if account&.public_key.blank?

    from_legacy_account(account, uri: uri)
  end

  def self.from_legacy_account(account, uri: nil)
    Keypair.new(
      account:,
      uri: uri.presence || ActivityPub::TagManager.instance.key_uri_for(account),
      public_key: account.public_key,
      private_key: account.private_key,
      type: :rsa

#  updated_at     :datetime         not null
#  account_id     :bigint(8)        not null

class Keypair < ApplicationRecord
  include Expireable

  self.inheritance_column = nil

  encrypts :private_key

  belongs_to :account

  enum :type, {
    rsa: 0,
    ed25519: 1,
    'ml-dsa-44': 2,
  }, validate: true

  validates :uri, presence: true, uniqueness: true, if: -> { account.remote? }
  validates :uri, absence: true, if: -> { account.local? }

  validates :local_fragment, presence: true, uniqueness: { scope: :account_id }, format: { with: /\A#[A-Z0-9-]+\Z/i }, if: -> { account.local? }
  validates :local_fragment, absence: true, if: -> { account.remote? }

  validates :public_key, presence: true
  validates :private_key, presence: true, if: -> { account.local? }
  validates :private_key, absence: true, if: -> { account.remote? }

  scope :unexpired, -> { where(expires_at: nil).or(where.not(expires_at: ..Time.now.utc)) }
  scope :usable, -> { unexpired.where(revoked: false) }

  alias actor account

  def full_uri
    return ActivityPub::TagManager.instance.uri_for(account) + local_fragment if local_fragment.present?

    uri
  end

  def keypair
    @keypair ||= begin
      case type
      when 'rsa'
        OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.new(private_key || public_key)
      when 'ed25519', 'ml-dsa-44'
        OpenSSL::PKey.read(private_key || public_key)
      end
    end
  end

  def linzer_public_key
    @linzer_public_key ||= begin
      case type
      when 'rsa'
        Linzer.new_rsa_v1_5_sha256_public_key(public_key)
      when 'ed25519'
        Linzer.new_ed25519_public_key(public_key)
      end
    end
  end

  def linzer_private_key
    @linzer_private_key ||= begin
      case type
      when 'rsa'
        Linzer.new_rsa_v1_5_sha256_key(private_key, full_uri)
      when 'ed25519'
        Linzer.new_ed25519_key(private_key, full_uri)
      end
    end
  end

  def usable?
    !revoked? && !expired?
  end

  def self.from_keyid(uri)
    return if uri.blank?

    keypair = find_by(uri: uri)
    return keypair unless keypair.nil?

    # No keypair found, try the old way we used to store RSA keypairs
    account = ActivityPub::TagManager.instance.uri_to_actor(uri)
    return if account&.public_key.blank?

    from_legacy_account(account, uri: uri)
  end

  def self.from_legacy_account(account, uri: nil)
    Keypair.new(
      account:,
      uri: uri.presence || ActivityPub::TagManager.instance.key_uri_for(account),
      public_key: account.public_key,
      private_key: account.private_key,
      type: :rsa
    )
  end

  def self.from_worker_arg(account, private_key_pem_or_hash)
    if private_key_pem_or_hash.is_a?(String)
      account.keypairs.build(
        private_key: private_key_pem_or_hash,

        public_key: private_key_pem_or_hash['public_key'],
        uri: private_key_pem_or_hash['uri'],
        local_fragment: private_key_pem_or_hash['local_fragment'],
        type: private_key_pem_or_hash['type']
      )
    end
  end
end

**Fabricator Shenanigans: A Deep Dive into Optimization**

Okay, so I've been digging into the fabricators, and honestly, I'm seeing some significant opportunities for optimization here. Let's break down my thoughts.

First, those `Account#generate_keys` lines—lines 351–367 and 559–564 in `app/models/account.rb`—are making me realize how important the pre-population of `keypairs` is. That setup with `SigningKeysHelpers::PUBLIC_RSA_TEST_KEY` and `PRIVATE_RSA_TEST_KEY` in `account_fabricator.rb` is crucial to prevent on-the-fly key generation, which impacts the speed of the keypair creation. I see that this supports ActivityPub requests correctly.

Then, there's the `Keypair` class itself, with that `encrypts :private_key`. It encrypts the key with AES-GCM *every single time* a `Keypair` is instantiated with the test keys, which is important to remember. But it's those double validations within the `keypairs` association—before and after the `accounts` insertion—that are a little inefficient.

Now, let's look at the fabricators in `spec/fabricators/`. My initial reaction is, "Whoa, there's a lot of unnecessary work going on here!"

#### Issue 1: `status_fabricator.rb` is a BIG one.

The `after_create` block in `status_fabricator.rb` is the main culprit. Fabricating a `Bookmark` *every single time* a `Status` is created is creating so many database queries, it is creating accounts for them to be attached to! Even the `after_build` block using `Faker::Internet.device_token` is unnecessary and costly—we can use a deterministic sequence instead.

#### Issue 2: `user_fabricator.rb` is next on the chopping block.

The `after_create` block in the `user_fabricator.rb` is creating **a ton** of unused `LoginActivity` rows. It is also calling `Faker` for the IP and User agent details. I'm seeing that the `email` field calls `Faker::Internet.email` way too often. I'm also concerned that we're making database calls for finding the `UserRole` roles. The use of `bypass_registration_checks` is also something to check. I need to figure out what tests rely on the default behavior and what tests depend on bypassing checks!

My immediate action plan is to assess:

1.  How to remove those `after_create` blocks creating redundant objects across the board.
2.  How to replace `Faker` calls with more efficient, deterministic values or sequences.
3.  How to optimize the loading of those `UserRole` instances.
4.  And, very importantly, whether changing `bypass_registration_checks` has any impact on the behavior of validation tests.

We can trim down the unnecessary work and shave some significant time off our test suite runtime!

**A Close Call with Email Domain Blocks!**

Oh, thank goodness we caught that! Looking back at lines 18 and 32 in `spec/models/email_domain_block_spec.rb`... that was a potential pitfall. If we had stuck with using something like `user#{i}@example.com` within `user_fabricator.rb`, any `Fabricate(:user)` call *after* a `Fabricate(:email_domain_block, domain: 'example.com')` would have immediately run afoul of that `EmailDomainBlock` on `example.com`!

But now, using `email { sequence(:email) { |i| "user#{i}@domain#{i}.test" } }` (or even `"user#{i}@user#{i}.example"`), ensures that *every* user gets a unique email domain: `domain#{i}.test`, for example, which will *never* collide with `'example.com'`, or `'other-example.com'`, or `mail.foo.com` for that matter!

Just to be absolutely certain, let's take another quick look at `spec/models/email_domain_block_spec.rb` just to make sure we didn't miss anything.

require 'resolv'

class EmailMxValidator < ActiveModel::EachValidator
  def validate_each(record, attribute, value)
    return if value.blank?

    domain = get_domain(value)

    if domain.blank? || domain.include?('..')
      record.errors.add(attribute, :invalid)
    elsif !on_allowlist?(domain)
      resolved_ips, resolved_domains = resolve_mx(domain)

      if resolved_ips.empty?
        record.errors.add(attribute, :unreachable)
      elsif email_domain_blocked?([domain, *resolved_domains], options[:attempt_ip].is_a?(Symbol) ? record.public_send(options[:attempt_ip]) : nil)
        record.errors.add(attribute, :blocked)
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def get_domain(value)
    _, domain = value.split('@', 2)

    return nil if domain.nil?

    TagManager.instance.normalize_domain(domain)
  rescue Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
    nil
  end

  def on_allowlist?(domain)
    return false if Rails.configuration.x.email_domains_allowlist.blank?

    Rails.configuration.x.email_domains_allowlist.include?(domain)
  end

  def resolve_mx(domain)
    records = []
    ips     = []

    Resolv::DNS.open do |dns|
      dns.timeouts = 5

      records = dns.getresources(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::MX).to_a.map { |e| e.exchange.to_s }
      next if records == [''] # This domain explicitly rejects emails

class UserEmailValidator < ActiveModel::Validator
  def validate(user)
    return if user.valid_invitation? || user.email.blank?

    user.errors.add(:email, :blocked) if blocked_email_provider?(user.email, user.sign_up_ip)
    user.errors.add(:email, :taken) if blocked_canonical_email?(user.email)
  end

  private

  def blocked_email_provider?(email, ip)
    disallowed_through_email_domain_block?(email, ip) || disallowed_through_configuration?(email) || not_allowed_through_configuration?(email)
  end

  def blocked_canonical_email?(email)
    CanonicalEmailBlock.block?(email)
  end

  def disallowed_through_email_domain_block?(email, ip)
    EmailDomainBlock.block?(email, attempt_ip: ip)
  end

  def not_allowed_through_configuration?(email)
    return false if Rails.configuration.x.email_domains_allowlist.blank?

    domains = Rails.configuration.x.email_domains_allowlist.gsub('.', '\.')
    regexp  = Regexp.new("@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})$", true)

    email !~ regexp
  end

  def disallowed_through_configuration?(email)
    return false if Rails.configuration.x.email_domains_denylist.blank?

    domains = Rails.configuration.x.email_domains_denylist.gsub('.', '\.')
    regexp  = Regexp.new("@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})", true)

    regexp.match?(email)
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class DomainValidator < ActiveModel::EachValidator
  MAX_DOMAIN_LENGTH = 256
  MIN_LABEL_LENGTH = 1
  MAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 63
  ALLOWED_CHARACTERS_RE = /^[a-z0-9-]+$/i

  def validate_each(record, attribute, value)
    return if value.blank?

    Array.wrap(value).each do |domain|
      if options[:acct]
        _, domain = domain.split('@')
        next if domain.blank?
      end

      record.errors.add(attribute, value.is_a?(Enumerable) ? :invalid_domain_on_line : :invalid, value: domain) unless compliant?(domain)
    end
  end

  private

  def compliant?(value)
    return false if value.blank?

    uri = Addressable::URI.new
    uri.host = value
    uri.normalized_host.size < MAX_DOMAIN_LENGTH && uri.normalized_host.split('.').all? { |label| label.size.between?(MIN_LABEL_LENGTH, MAX_LABEL_LENGTH) && label =~ ALLOWED_CHARACTERS_RE }
  rescue Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError, IDN::Idna::IdnaError
    false
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class ExistingUsernameValidator < ActiveModel::EachValidator
  def validate_each(record, attribute, value)
    @value = value
    return if @value.blank?

    if options[:multiple]
      record.errors.add(attribute, not_found_multiple_message) if usernames_with_no_accounts.any?
    elsif usernames_with_no_accounts.any? || usernames_and_domains.size > 1
      record.errors.add(attribute, not_found_message)
    end
  end

  private

  def usernames_and_domains
    @value.split(',').filter_map do |string|
      username, domain = string.strip.gsub(/\A@/, '').split('@', 2)
      domain = nil if TagManager.instance.local_domain?(domain)

      next if username.blank?

      [string, username, domain]
    end
  end

  def usernames_with_no_accounts
    usernames_and_domains.filter_map do |(string, username, domain)|
      string unless Account.find_remote(username, domain)
    end
  end

  def not_found_multiple_message
    I18n.t('existing_username_validator.not_found_multiple', usernames: usernames_with_no_accounts.join(', '))
  end

  def not_found_message
    I18n.t('existing_username_validator.not_found')
  end
end

**Analyzing Account Conversation Fabricator Optimization**

Okay, let's break this down. I need to optimize the `account_conversation.rb` and `account_conversation_fabricator.rb` files. Looking at `account_conversation.rb`, I see the expected `belongs_to` relationships with `account`, `conversation`, and `last_status`. That `last_status` association is particularly interesting, set via `before_validation :set_last_status` using the last element of `status_ids`. A crucial point is that every `Status` instance already inherently creates its own `Conversation` and links back to an `account`.

Now, the `account_conversation_fabricator.rb` is where things are inefficient. Currently, the fabricator does the following:

messages.thinking:
**The Curious Case of the Null `account_id`**

Aha! `spec/fabrication` really shined here! It immediately pinpointed the root cause of that puzzling `account_id = null` on the `Poll` model. Time to delve into *why* this happened.

Okay, so I see it. In `app/models/status.rb`, the `Status` model `belongs_to :poll`. This is a crucial clue because the `polls` table *also* has a `status_id`, and the `statuses` table has a `poll_id`.

Here's the sequence: If a `poll` is fabricated with an *unpersisted* `account` (like with `Fabricate.build(:account)`) and an *unpersisted* `status` (`Fabricate.build(:status, account: attrs[:account])`), then, upon calling `Poll#save!`, ActiveRecord's save order is the key. It first saves the `Poll`'s `belongs_to :status`. This, in turn, saves the `status.account`, which *at that moment* assigns an `account.id`. However, because `Status` has a `has_one :poll` relationship *and* `belongs_to :poll`, this triggers a `Poll` insert *before* the `Poll`'s own `belongs_to :account` association is processed through `autosave_associated_records_for_account`. This is the crux of the problem: the `poll.account_id` isn't populated!

Conversely, if the `account` is already persisted on the `Poll`— which occurs when we used `account { |attrs| attrs[:status]&.account || Fabricate(:account) }` — then the `account.id` is *already* non-null when it is assigned to both `poll.account` and `status.account`, solving the issue.

And, bonus, `spec/fabrication`'s performance is already dramatically improved from 6.86 seconds to 4.67 seconds!

Now, let's rigorously test that fix using `account { |attrs| attrs[:status]&.account || Fabricate(:account) }` in `poll_fabricator.rb`. We also need to check `status_pin_fabricator.rb`, given that `status_pin` passed in `spec/fabrication` – so far, so good – and, to be extra sure, verify both `Fabricate(:poll)` and `Fabricate.build(:poll)` scenarios.

module PerFileFactoryProfiler
  mattr_accessor :current_file, default: 'boot'
  mattr_accessor :stats, default: Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = { calls: 0, builds: 0, time: 0.0, examples: 0 } }
  mattr_accessor :depth, default: 0
end

RSpec.configure do |config|
  config.around(:each) do |ex|
    PerFileFactoryProfiler.current_file = ex.metadata[:file_path]
    PerFileFactoryProfiler.stats[ex.metadata[:file_path]][:examples] += 1
    ex.run
  end

  config.before(:context) do |ctx|
    PerFileFactoryProfiler.current_file = ctx.class.metadata[:file_path]
  end

  config.after(:suite) do
    puts "\n=== TOP 25 FILES BY FACTORY TIME ==="
    PerFileFactoryProfiler.stats.sort_by { |_, v| -v[:time] }.first(25).each do |file, v|
      printf "%6.3fs  calls:%4d  builds:%4d  ex:%3d  %s\n", v[:time], v[:calls], v[:builds], v[:examples], file
    end
  end
end

Fabrication::Schematic::Definition.prepend(Module.new do

    if PerFileFactoryProfiler.depth == 0
      PerFileFactoryProfiler.depth += 1
      t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
      begin
        super
      ensure
        dt = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t0
        PerFileFactoryProfiler.depth -= 1
        s = PerFileFactoryProfiler.stats[PerFileFactoryProfiler.current_file]
        s[:calls] += 1
        s[:time] += dt
      end
    else
      super
    end
  end

  def build(*, **)
    if PerFileFactoryProfiler.depth == 0

        s[:builds] += 1

end)

class NotificationRequest < ApplicationRecord
  self.ignored_columns += %w(dismissed)

  include Paginable

  MAX_MEANINGFUL_COUNT = 100

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :from_account, class_name: 'Account'
  belongs_to :last_status, class_name: 'Status'

  before_save :prepare_notifications_count

  scope :without_suspended, -> { joins(:from_account).merge(Account.without_suspended) }

  def self.preload_cache_collection(requests)
    cached_statuses_by_id = yield(requests.filter_map(&:last_status)).index_by(&:id) # Call cache_collection in block

    requests.each do |request|
      request.last_status = cached_statuses_by_id[request.last_status_id] unless request.last_status_id.nil?
    end
  end

  def reconsider_existence!
    prepare_notifications_count

    if notifications_count.positive?
      save
    else
      destroy
    end
  end

  private

  def prepare_notifications_count
    self.notifications_count = Notification.where(account: account, from_account: from_account, type: [:mention, :quote], filtered: true).limit(MAX_MEANINGFUL_COUNT).count
  end
end

class Conversation < ApplicationRecord

class AnnouncementReaction < ApplicationRecord
  before_validation :set_custom_emoji, if: :name?
  after_commit :queue_publish

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :announcement, inverse_of: :announcement_reactions
  belongs_to :custom_emoji, optional: true

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates_with ReactionValidator

  private

  def set_custom_emoji
    self.custom_emoji = CustomEmoji.local.enabled.find_by(shortcode: name)
  end

  def queue_publish
    PublishAnnouncementReactionWorker.perform_async(announcement_id, name) unless announcement.destroyed?
  end
end
# frozen_string_literal: true

class ReactionValidator < ActiveModel::Validator
  SUPPORTED_EMOJIS = JSON.load_file(Rails.root.join('app', 'javascript', 'mastodon', 'features', 'emoji', 'emoji_map.json').to_s).keys.freeze

  LIMIT = 8

  def validate(reaction)
    return if reaction.name.blank?

    reaction.errors.add(:name, I18n.t('reactions.errors.unrecognized_emoji')) if reaction.custom_emoji_id.blank? && !unicode_emoji?(reaction.name)
    reaction.errors.add(:base, I18n.t('reactions.errors.limit_reached')) if new_reaction?(reaction) && limit_reached?(reaction)
  end

  private

  def unicode_emoji?(name)
    SUPPORTED_EMOJIS.include?(name)
  end

  def new_reaction?(reaction)
    !reaction.announcement.announcement_reactions.exists?(name: reaction.name)
  end

  def limit_reached?(reaction)
    reaction.announcement.announcement_reactions.where.not(name: reaction.name).count('distinct name') >= LIMIT
  end
end

require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe AnnouncementReaction do
  describe 'Associations' do
    it { is_expected.to belong_to(:account) }
    it { is_expected.to belong_to(:announcement).inverse_of(:announcement_reactions) }
    it { is_expected.to belong_to(:custom_emoji).optional }
  end

  describe 'Validations' do
    subject { Fabricate.build :announcement_reaction }

    it { is_expected.to validate_presence_of(:name) }
    it { is_expected.to allow_values('😀').for(:name) }
    it { is_expected.to_not allow_values('INVALID').for(:name) }

    context 'when reaction limit is reached' do
      subject { Fabricate.build :announcement_reaction, announcement: announcement_reaction.announcement }

      let(:announcement_reaction) { Fabricate :announcement_reaction, name: '😊' }

      before { stub_const 'ReactionValidator::LIMIT', 1 }

      it { is_expected.to_not allow_values('😀').for(:name).against(:base) }
    end
  end

  describe 'Callbacks' do
    describe 'Setting custom emoji association' do
      subject { Fabricate.build :announcement_reaction, name: }

      context 'when name is missing' do
        let(:name) { '' }

        it 'does not set association' do
          expect { subject.valid? }
            .to not_change(subject, :custom_emoji).from(be_blank)
        end
      end

      context 'when name matches a custom emoji shortcode' do
        let(:name) { 'custom' }
        let!(:custom_emoji) { Fabricate :custom_emoji, shortcode: 'custom' }

        it 'sets association' do
          expect { subject.valid? }
            .to change(subject, :custom_emoji).from(be_blank).to(custom_emoji)
        end
      end

      context 'when name does not match a custom emoji' do
        let(:name) { 'custom' }

        it 'does not set association' do
          expect { subject.valid? }
            .to not_change(subject, :custom_emoji).from(be_blank)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe AnnouncementReaction do
  describe 'Associations' do
    it { is_expected.to belong_to(:account) }
    it { is_expected.to belong_to(:announcement).inverse_of(:announcement_reactions) }
    it { is_expected.to belong_to(:custom_emoji).optional }
  end

  describe 'Validations' do
    subject { Fabricate.build :announcement_reaction }

    it { is_expected.to validate_presence_of(:name) }
    it { is_expected.to allow_values('😀').for(:name) }
    it { is_expected.to_not allow_values('INVALID').for(:name) }

    context 'when reaction limit is reached' do
      subject { Fabricate.build :announcement_reaction, announcement: announcement_reaction.announcement }

      let(:announcement_reaction) { Fabricate :announcement_reaction, name: '😊' }

      before { stub_const 'ReactionValidator::LIMIT', 1 }

      it { is_expected.to_not allow_values('😀').for(:name).against(:base) }
    end
  end

  describe 'Callbacks' do
    describe 'Setting custom emoji association' do
      subject { Fabricate.build :announcement_reaction, name: }

      context 'when name is missing' do
        let(:name) { '' }

        it 'does not set association' do
          expect { subject.valid? }
            .to not_change(subject, :custom_emoji).from(be_blank)
        end
      end

      context 'when name matches a custom emoji shortcode' do
        let(:name) { 'custom' }
        let!(:custom_emoji) { Fabricate :custom_emoji, shortcode: 'custom' }

        it 'sets association' do
          expect { subject.valid? }
            .to change(subject, :custom_emoji).from(be_blank).to(custom_emoji)
        end
      end

      context 'when name does not match a custom emoji' do
        let(:name) { 'custom' }

        it 'does not set association' do
          expect { subject.valid? }
            .to not_change(subject, :custom_emoji).from(be_blank)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

Hang on a minute! `Fabricate(:user)` *already* creates an `account` associated with the user. Then the second `let` statement just goes and *re-fabricates* an `account` and overwrites the original, right? I mean, `user.account` is already there! This is a classic case of unnecessary duplication, and I hate when that sneaks in.

A much cleaner and more elegant solution would be to use `include_context 'with API authentication'` and simply define the account as `let(:account) { user.account }`. This gives the same setup, and would streamline the tests in those specs.

**The Root of the Issue**

Aha! I've spotted it, the culprit! That failure in `spec/requests/api/v2/admin/accounts_spec.rb:105` is now crystal clear. The problem lies in the ordering within `api/v2/admin/accounts_spec.rb`. Initially, we had a setup where several account fixtures, `remote_account`, `other_remote_account`, `suspended_account`, `suspended_remote`, `disabled_account`, `pending_account` were defined using `let!`, followed by `admin_account` which depended on a lazy `user` defined with `let(:user)`.

Because `user` was lazy-loaded with `let(:user)`, `admin_account` ended up being created **last**, giving it the highest `id`. This caused the `limit: 1` query (ordered by `id DESC`) to erroneously select `admin_account` first. The `max_id` was effectively equal to the `admin_account.id`!

Furthermore, when the `include_context 'with API authentication'` block was executed at the top of the `RSpec.describe`, `user` was initialized with `let_it_be(:user)` and was created **first**, getting the lowest `id`. This introduced a discrepancy that broke the expectations.

My solution is to move the definition of the accounts using `let_it_be` *before* the inclusion of the API authentication context *within the `describe 'GET #index'` block*. This will ensure that `user` gets created **last**, with the highest `id`, just like the original intention! Let's verify that this resolves the issue immediately.

phase3 = """
## Phase 3: Factories (`spec/fabricators/`) & Factory Usage in `spec/models` and `spec/requests`

### Post-Phase-2 vs. After Phase 3 Metrics

| Metric | Post-Phase-2 | After Phase 3 | Phase 3 Change | Cumulative vs. Original Baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/fabrication` (115 ex, `Fabricate.times(2, ...)`) | **6.86s** | **3.84s** | **~44.0% faster** | — |
| `spec/models` wall-clock (1,795 ex) | **30.63s** | **21.20s–22.58s** (avg ~21.89s) | **~28.5% faster** | **~83.5% faster (~6.0x)** vs. 132.3s |
| `spec/requests` wall-clock (1,877 ex) | **55.03s** (~48.0s–55.0s) | **39.69s–44.03s** (avg ~41.60s) | **~24.4% faster** | **>79% faster (~4.8x)** vs. >200s (**~3.35x** vs. 139.4s Post-Phase-1) |
| **Combined `spec/models` + `spec/requests`** | **85.66s** (~79.9s–85.7s) | **~63.49s** (`21.89s` + `41.60s`) | **~25.9% faster** | **>5.2x faster** vs. >330s Baseline |
| `spec/models` FactoryProf (`Fabricate` calls / time) | 2,869 calls / **31.35s** | 2,119 calls / **17.30s–18.42s** | **-26.1% calls / ~43% less time** | **-55.1% calls / ~84% less time** vs. 4,721 / 114.6s |
| `spec/requests` FactoryProf (`Fabricate` calls / time) | 3,899 calls / **29.91s** | 2,315 calls / **12.02s** | **-40.6% calls / ~59.8% less time** | **-79.0% calls / ~88.7% less time** vs. 11,030 / 106.7s |
| `spec/models` `sql.active_record` events / SQL time | 45,229 / 8.75s | 35,364 / 4.96s | **-21.8% queries / -43.3% SQL time** | **-69.0% queries** vs. 113,956 |
| `spec/requests` `sql.active_record` events / SQL time | 79,455 / 13.73s | 67,646 / 6.66s | **-14.9% queries / -51.5% SQL time** | — |

#### Per-Factory Cost Reductions (`FactoryProf` time per call)

| Factory | Post-Phase-2 | After Phase 3 | Improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:status` | 25.8ms (`models`) / 28.6ms (`requests`) | **7.9ms** (`models`) / **7.5ms** (`requests`) | **~70–74% faster (~3.5x)** |
| `:user` | 19.3ms (`models`) / 16.2ms (`requests`) | **7.8ms** (`models`) / **7.2ms** (`requests`) | **~56–60% faster (~2.3x)** |
| `:account` | 11.2ms (`models`) / 11.1ms (`requests`) | **7.6ms** (`models`) / **6.5ms** (`requests`) | **~32–41% faster** |
| `:poll` | 17.5ms | **4.0ms** | **~77% faster (~4.4x)** |
| `:custom_filter_status` | 20.3ms | **4.9ms** | **~76% faster (~4.1x)** |
| `:notification_request` | 34.6ms (`models`) / 29.5ms (`requests`) | **15.5ms** (`models`) / **12.2ms** (`requests`) | **~55–59% faster** |
| `:canonical_email_block` | 10.8ms | **0.9ms** | **~92% faster (~12x)** |
| `:conversation` | 14.5ms | **0.8ms** | **~94.5% faster (~18x)** |
| `:report_note` | 14.3ms | **2.2ms** | **~85% faster (~6.5x)** |

---

### Root Causes Identified & Fixed in Phase 3

1. **Unconditional `after_create { Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status) }` in `spec/fabricators/status_fabricator.rb`**
   - `StackProf` showed this single callback accounted for **17.0% of all example wall time in `spec/models`** (4,886 / 28,697 samples) and **8.6% in `spec/requests`** (3,886 / 45,281 samples).
   - Every `Fabricate(:status)` secretly created a `Bookmark` + a second `Account` + a second `User` + a second `Keypair` (~20 extra SQL queries per status), responsible for 441 of 445 bookmarks in `spec/models` and 339 of 348 bookmarks in `spec/requests`.
   - **Fix**: Removed the `after_create` hook from `status_fabricator.rb`; every spec testing bookmarks already explicitly fabricates `:bookmark`.

2. **Unconditional `after_create { 2.times { Fabricate(:login_activity, user: user) } }` in `spec/fabricators/user_fabricator.rb`**
   - Created 256 unused `LoginActivity` rows in `spec/models` and 882 in `spec/requests`.
   - **Fix**: Removed the `after_create` hook from `user_fabricator.rb`.

3. **Unnecessary Optional & Duplicate Cascading `Account` / `CustomEmoji` Associations Across Fabricators**
   - **Note on `Account#user` & `Account#keypairs` (must be kept)**: Local `Account` records (`domain.nil?`) **must** keep `user` (`Account.without_unapproved` and `Account.search_for` join `users` on `approved = TRUE AND confirmed_at IS NOT NULL`, and ~40 model/request specs access `account.user`) and `keypairs` (prevents `Account#generate_keys` from generating 2048-bit RSA keys and satisfies `Keypair.from_keyid` / `ActivityPub::ActorSerializer` specs).
   - However, several other fabricators built optional or duplicate `Account` / `CustomEmoji` graphs that no spec implicitly depended on:
     - `canonical_email_block_fabricator.rb`: removed optional `reference_account { Fabricate.build(:account) }` (eliminated 39 `Account` + `User` + `Keypair` creations).
     - `conversation_fabricator.rb`: removed optional `parent_account { Fabricate(:account) }`.
     - `announcement_reaction_fabricator.rb`: defaulted `name` to Unicode emoji `'\U0001f44d'` instead of `Fabricate(:custom_emoji).shortcode` (avoiding `CustomEmoji` + Paperclip image assignment unless explicitly requested).
     - `poll_fabricator.rb`, `status_pin_fabricator.rb`, `status_trend_fabricator.rb`, `notification_request_fabricator.rb`, `custom_filter_status_fabricator.rb`, `account_conversation_fabricator.rb`, and `report_note_fabricator.rb`: wired `account` / `status` / `conversation` attributes to share the same `Account` (and respect passed-in overrides via `attrs[...]`) instead of fabricating 2–3 separate `Account` + `User` + `Keypair` trees per record. Note: on `Poll`, `StatusTrend`, `NotificationRequest`, and `CustomFilterStatus`, the shared parent association uses `Fabricate(...)` so foreign-key IDs are populated before ActiveRecord saves bidirectional associations (while `Fabricate.build(...)` on the outer factory still automatically converts nested `Fabricate(...)` calls to `build` via `Fabrication.manager.build_stack`).

4. **Precomputed EC Keys & Deterministic Sequences Replacing `Faker` + `I18n` Lookups**
   - Precomputed `prime256v1` EC keys once at load time in `web_push_subscription_fabricator.rb` and `webauthn_credential_fabricator.rb` instead of calling `OpenSSL::PKey::EC.generate(\x27prime256v1\x27)` per record.
   - Replaced `Faker::Internet.*` / `Faker::Lorem.*` / `Faker::Date.unique.*` calls across 23 fabricators (`account`, `user`, `status`, `tag`, `domain_block`, `email_domain_block`, `unavailable_domain`, `preview_card`, `preview_card_provider`, `canonical_email_block`, `email_subscription`, `username_block`, `instance_moderation_note`, `login_activity`, `fasp_provider`, `terms_of_service`, `tagged_object`, `webhook`, `rule`, `appeal`, `account_warning`, `account_warning_preset`, `announcement`, `account_moderation_note`) with fast deterministic sequences using non-colliding prefixes/TLDs (`acct_#{i}`, `acct_#{i}@mail-#{i}.test`, `hashtag#{i}`, `domain-#{i}.test`) so they never collide with search terms (`test`, `username`, `match`) or `example.com` blocklist fixtures.

5. **OAuth Token Reuse & Remaining Per-Example Factory Setup in `spec/requests` and `spec/models`**
   - Updated `shared_context \x27with API authentication\x27` (`spec/support/api_authentication.rb`) to update `oauth_token` scopes in-place within the example transaction (`update_columns(scopes: ...)`) when `scopes` is overridden (such as in 180+ `forbidden for wrong scope` shared examples), cutting `Fabricate(:accessible_access_token)` calls in `spec/requests` from 429 to 170.
   - Migrated remaining manual per-example OAuth/account fixture setups in `api/v2/admin/accounts_spec.rb`, `api/v2/filters/statuses_spec.rb`, `api/v2/filters/keywords_spec.rb`, `oauth/userinfo_spec.rb`, `api/v1/featured_tags/suggestions_spec.rb`, `api/v1/domain_blocks/previews_spec.rb`, `api/v2/search_spec.rb`, and `models/account_suggestions/friends_of_friends_source_spec.rb` to `with API authentication` and `let_it_be` (and removed redundant `Fabricate(:account, user: user)` calls where `user.account` already existed).

---

## Insights for Future Phases (`spec/services`, `spec/controllers`, `spec/workers`, `spec/serializers`)

- All Phase 3 fabricator optimizations automatically speed up **every** other spec directory (`spec/services`, `spec/controllers`, `spec/workers`, `spec/serializers`, `spec/presenters`, `spec/policies`, `spec/lib`) because `Fabricate(:status)`, `Fabricate(:user)`, and `Fabricate(:account)` are 32–74% faster globally.
- If optimizing `spec/controllers`, `spec/services`, `spec/serializers`, or `spec/workers` in future runs:
  - Extending `:paperclip_processing` (`spec/support/paperclip.rb`) and `:refresh_instances_view` (`spec/support/domain_materializable.rb`) defaults to those spec types (opting in via metadata tags only in specs testing image/video processing or `Instance` view refreshes) will avoid `vips`/`ffmpeg` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY instances` overhead there too.
  - Extending `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` default to `spec/controllers` and `spec/serializers` (and selectively to `spec/services` where inline worker execution isn\x27t under test) will eliminate `TriggerWebhookWorker` overhead in those directories just as it did in `spec/models` and `spec/requests`.
"""

with open("docs/RSPEC_OPTIMIZATION.md", "w") as f:
    f.write(kept + phase3)
' && rm -rf tmp/test_prof && git status -s
